# Original runtime signature observations

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz), [index](index.json) and
[validation record](validation.json) retain 93 original records. Seven complete
projects have fourteen actual ordinary/selected CLI observations: ordinary
enum/match controls succeed, quantum nominal execution reaches its concrete
profile barriers, and ordinary quantum inspection/hidden observation reach
their actual type/effect errors. The prior CLI and native executables are
hash-bound observations, without current-head build attestation.

The new internal reader retains complete runtime prefixes around quantum
owners, including nested products and ordinary zero-width parameters. It reuses
the original finite-type and import readers; an annotation read is not a checked
body effect. The first reserved `Type` identifier error and separate default-list
projection error remain unchanged. Separate repairs compile with strict package
options; 22 small kernel reductions and a 21,130-declaration audit pass using
only the existing standard axiom basis. Single-process peak memory is about
1.65 GiB. No maximum-size quantum case is generated.

Original observers, source objects, complete diagnostic streams and source/import
maps remain inert data. Passive tests neither extract nor replay them. These
component compiles use stable existing imports and do not establish a full
dependency replay, source-body theorem or native execution gate. Current proof
records require genuine maintenance for this candidate. Ordinary/selected typed
execution, complete body/code/effect binding and generic/static transport remain
unfinished; #64 and #195 remain open.

The archived observer initially reports 23 reductions; enumerating the actual
theorem declarations gives 22. The separate validation record corrects that
count without rewriting the original observer or its archive.

## Mixed runtime root component

The separate [root archive](runtime-root-first.tar.xz),
[root index](runtime-root-index.json) and [root validation](runtime-root-validation.json)
retain 130 records without altering the signature history above. Four desired
programs have eight real prior-CLI observations: six concrete profile barriers
and two actual hidden-discard effect refusals. These are informed integration
inputs, not an independent initial-authoring study or current native attestation.

First storage, missing exact-composition API, annotation-decidability and test
elaboration failures remain alongside separate repairs. The compiled audit's
generated partial-recursion refusal is retained; a bounded Nat recursion and
generic complete-history-length theorem repair it without relaxing the audit.
The corrected component compiles 24 small kernel reductions, evaluates all 21
mixed-root controls and audits 21,637 declarations with only the existing
standard axiom basis. The observed single-process peak is 905,428,992 bytes
(about 0.84 GiB). New cases use at most three physical bits.

The root retains original full type queries, exact ordinary storage, ordered
quantum ports and the same freshly validated Raw graph. Independent canonical
ordinary inputs and every hidden quantum history receive storage/code checks,
including zero-probability results. Lifted exact logical maps must equal their
actual physical maps; their complete Gram sum is checked. A generic theorem
rules out a rectangular logical Unitary label. Public Observe is not sharpened.
This is actual-IR typing and exact-computation evidence, not an arbitrary
algorithm request, complex-denotation or source/runtime preservation theorem.

Current native/QDV dispatch and normal project/selected execution do not use
this component yet. Generic/static and wider qmatch integration, complete fresh
package replay, genuine proof-record maintenance and hosted CI/review remain
required. #64/#195 stay open; no new guarantee or release is claimed. Historical
observers and sources are never executed or extracted by retention tests.
